posts.title: Progression without evolution
posts.excerpt: What would we be without Evolution? Just Mayhem.
posts.body:
Actually, the very first progression idea for this game was exactly what is now called Evolution mode. When a player dies, they go into the next fight with a new action that might give them an edge. I love mechanics like this - the "natural selection" element is something I try to work into designs wherever I can.

But.

When we started playtesting, it turned out - and this is the paradox - that the most fun matches were the ones where you couldn't push each other off the board. The mechanic I built the whole progression system around was making the game less enjoyable. No eliminations means rounds go long - which means Evolution just doesn't fit, because players get tired without constant progression. In those conditions a new action would only show up once every 10–15 minutes, and by then you've already lost interest.
So I had to put my original idea aside. Not throw it out though. I wrote it down alongside the Mayhem system I'm using now, and honestly I'm counting on it. Evolution mode is still coming - just not for the exam deadline. I won't make it in time.


The natural selection is coming

posts.title: Prediction against Synergy
posts.excerpt: Getting actions to synergise turned out to be exactly as hard as I expected. And that's not good
posts.body:
Synergy between actions was one of the things I was most excited about designing. Two abilities that each do something small, but together do something surprising - that's the dream.

In practice it's been the hardest thing to get right.

The issue is that Read Me already asks a lot from the player on the prediction side. You're committing a full action chain without seeing your opponent's. Add a strong synergy on top of that and suddenly you're not just predicting what they'll do - you're predicting whether they've figured out your combo, and whether they're playing around it, and whether you should fake it this round.

That's interesting in theory. In playtests it was mostly just confusing.
The abilities that survived testing are the ones that synergise subtly - where the interaction is something you discover over several games. Getting there took killing a lot of things that felt clever on the board but fell apart when two real people were playing.


When I play against myself everything works much better...

posts.title: Prototyping of "Read Me"
posts.excerpt: How do I see my upcoming game and what are my next steps.
posts.body:
In this project I'm trying to mix the Synergy and Prediction mechanics into one game.

During prototyping I focused on the Prediction and wanted to be sure, that the main mechanic of reading your opponent works well in this concept and that the game loop makes prediction feel meaningful and rewarding. I believe I managed to achieve this feeling and I can move forward and experiment a bit with different actions that players could find interesting to interact with.

Once I have a pool of working, interesting and fun actions that fit the concept, I’ll be able to move on to adding progression to the gameplay. And on this stage I aim to keep the different actions synergistic so the game remains engaging throughout and offers replayability.

Stay tuned for more updates.

### You can find the Read Me page by clicking the game card in the "Upcoming Projects" section. Any feedback is very welcome.
